audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant, final (final stress)' rests on the 2016 ANU grammar, the most recent and fullest description (Glottolog lists only it and its 1957 Dutch source). We held no copy; I downloaded the open-access PDF and confirmed the deciding quotation verbatim in sec. 1.2.3 (printed p. 21, record says p. 22 — off by one, section spans 21-22). The grammar's further stress remarks (regular suffix-final stress in verbs, lexical exceptions marked with grave accent, clitic/suffix-induced shifts, N1PL realis stem-final stress) support 'dominant, not strict' final stress. Caveat inherent to the language, not the record: all data are Drabbe's 1950s impressionistic transcription ('weak accent'); no instrumental or later fieldwork exists. Optional housekeeping: register the downloaded PDF as the copy we hold and correct the locator to p. 21-22.

sources.citation: van den Heuvel 2016, Aghu (A-PL 33), full PDF from ANU repository, sec. 1.2.3 p. 22
sources.quote: Lexical stress is on the last syllable of the word. Drabbe speaks of a "weak accent." Following Drabbe, I have not indicated stress in case it is regular, and use an accent grave to indicate stress in irregular cases, as in toxopòmu 'some'.

sources.citation: van den Heuvel, Wilco. 2016. Aghu: annotated texts with grammatical introduction and vocabulary lists. Asia-Pacific Linguistics 33. Canberra: Australian National University. hdl:1885/111412 (open access).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: "Lexical stress is on the last syllable of the word. Drabbe speaks of a 'weak accent.' Following Drabbe, I have not indicated stress in case it is regular, and use an accent grave to indicate stress in irregular cases, as in toxopòmu 'some'. Scattered over the book, Drabbe gives several examples of stress shift to the prefinal syllable caused by 'a strong connection between a word and another element.'"
sources.locator: sec. 1.2.3 'Lexical stress', printed p. 21 (PDF p. 39), continuing p. 22; also sec. 2.3.1 p. ~31 ('Stress is generally regular, on the final vowel of the suffix.. exception.. N1PL realis forms, where stress is on the final syllable of the stem')
